Parametric bootstrap for a ga_fit

Source: R/ga_bootstrap.R
ga_bootstrap.Rd

Simulates B data sets from the fitted model with ga_simulate(), that is, from the Markov jump process and the observation model assumed by ga_loglik(), refits each by ga_fit() started at the estimates, and records a statistic of every refit. Missing values in the original data are kept missing in the simulated data sets, and rates that vary between blocks are simulated with their block values.

Usage

ga_bootstrap(
  fit,
  B = 200,
  statistic = stats::coef,
  init_counts = NULL,
  cores = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  maxit = 1500
)

Arguments

fit

A ga_fit() result.

B

Number of bootstrap replicates.

statistic

Function of a ga_fit returning a named numeric vector, applied to fit and to every refit. The default returns the estimates.

init_counts

Named vector of initial counts per compartment, summing to the population size of the fit. By default the initial fractions at the estimates times the population size, rounded, with the rounding remainder added to the largest compartment.

cores

Number of processes for parallel::mclapply(), which forks; use 1 on Windows.

seed

Optional seed set before the replicate seeds are drawn.

maxit

Nelder-Mead iteration limit of each refit.

Value

An object of class ga_boot with elements t0 (statistic at fit), t (matrix with one row per replicate, NA where the simulation or the refit failed), loglik and convergence (the optim code of each refit) and init_counts.

Details

Each replicate draws its own seed from the current random-number stream, so the result is reproducible under set.seed() (or seed) and does not depend on cores.

See also

confint.ga_boot(), ga_profile().

Examples

# \donttest{
sir <- ga_model(c("S", "I", "R"), list(
  infection = ga_event("S", "I", "lambda", by = "I"),
  removal   = ga_event("I", "R", "gamma")))
obs <- list(cases = ga_incidence("infection", prob = "p", noise = "tau2"))
set.seed(1)
sim <- ga_simulate(sir, list(lambda = 0.5, gamma = 0.2, p = 0.5, tau2 = 0.1),
                   c(S = 4990, I = 10, R = 0), obs, n = 60)
init <- function(p) c(S = 1 - p$i0, I = p$i0, R = 0)
fit <- ga_fit(sir, sim$data, obs, 5000, init,
              start = list(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.25, i0 = 0.005, p = 0.4, tau2 = 0.2))
bt <- ga_bootstrap(fit, B = 20, seed = 2)
confint(bt)
#>               2.5 %      97.5 %
#> lambda 3.113220e-01 0.534183195
#> gamma  5.521845e-02 0.246993159
#> i0     1.283805e-03 0.005556414
#> p      4.402647e-01 0.530667869
#> tau2   6.413786e-07 0.423937863
# }
